metaTitle: TGPORTAL — Telegram ↔ Delta Chat media bridge
metaDescription: Pair once, then stickers, GIFs, Lottie, and short video move both ways. Prefer self-hosting: you trust whoever runs the bot.
warnBody: A public bot is a relay. Whoever runs tgportal can see pairing data and everything you bridge. Delta Chat encryption does not hide messages from that host. Prefer self-hosting so you are the only operator.
heroTitle: Stickers and GIFs that survive the jump to Delta Chat.
heroLead: TGPORTAL is a Go bridge. Pair once with a short code. After that, media you send the Telegram bot lands in your Delta Chat conversation — and the other way around — without noisy filenames or “from Telegram” captions.
posterAlt: TGPORTAL branding poster: dark void with the product mark
bridgeLead: Bidirectional, per-user pairing. Telegram types stay useful on Delta Chat.

media.dc: File, or GIF if a converter is installed

howLead: Default product: one Telegram user maps to one Delta Chat chat on the portal bot. Use a live instance only if you accept trusting that host. You can also start from Delta Chat and open t.me/…?start=CODE.

steps.title: Open the Telegram bot
steps.body: Message @tgdeltabridgebot and send /start in a private chat.

steps.title: Open the Delta Chat invite
steps.body: The bot replies with an invite QR/link and a short pairing code (about 30 minutes).

steps.title: Send the code on Delta Chat
steps.body: Accept the chat, send only the code. The pair becomes active: your Telegram user ↔ that DC chat.

steps.title: Send media either way
steps.body: Stickers, GIFs, text, images, short video. Filenames stay neutral; source captions are stripped.

personaTitle: Persona: they message your Telegram bot. You see them as people on Delta Chat.
personaLead: Personal mode is one public portal bot and one chat. Persona is different: you plug in a bot you created with BotFather. Friends never join a shared dump. Each Telegram user becomes a ghost — a real Delta Chat account with their name and photo — that opens a normal 1:1 with you. Replies you type there leave as your bot.
personalCardBody: You talk to the portal bot. Stickers and text land in one Delta Chat conversation with that bot. Fine for “my media, my chat.”
personaCardBody: They talk to your bot. On Delta Chat, Alice looks like Alice, Bob looks like Bob — separate chats, reused forever for the same Telegram id.
flowLead: Follow the dashed line from top to bottom. Each stop is one hop the message takes.

flow.title: Alice DMs your bot
flow.body: She never opens Delta Chat. She only knows the Telegram bot you published.

flow.title: TGPORTAL is polling it
flow.body: You registered the BotFather token with /pair-bot on the portal (after you /paired yourself).

flow.title: One DC account per Telegram id
flow.body: Missing? Create with PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR, copy name and photo. Exists? Reuse. Not the same table as personal pairs.

flow.title: Normal 1:1 on Delta Chat
flow.body: No “via Telegram” label. Your reply goes back out through the bot. Telegram cannot puppet Alice as Alice.

setupBody: mode: persona or both. Pair the portal so TGPORTAL has your DC public key. Then /pair-bot <TOKEN> in a private chat. Token stays in SQLite under ./data.
groupsBody: Turn on persona.allow_groups, add the bot, disable BotFather group privacy. Posts become a Delta Chat group TG: … with each speaker as their ghost. You are a member; your replies are the bot.
hostBody: Whoever runs tgportal holds the token and the ghost keys. Do not /pair-bot on a public instance you do not operate.
selfLead: This is the recommended way to use TGPORTAL. Open source (MIT). One Go binary plus deltachat-rpc-server on PATH. You hold the token, the SQLite DB, and the ghost keys.
selfNeeds: Go 1.22+ and a Telegram BotFather token
Chatmail / Delta Chat provider (e.g. nine.testrun.org for tests)
